title: Chi-Squared Law for Random-Permutation Capacity
summary: A plausibility argument supports a chi-squared law for the scaled linear-correlation capacity of a random permutation, but a formal proof remains open.

formal_statement.body: Let $P$ be a randomly chosen permutation of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and let $V\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n\times\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be any vector subspace. For masks $(\alpha,\beta)$, define $\operatorname{Cor}(P;\alpha,\beta)=\Pr_{x\leftarrow\mathbb{F}_2^n}[\alpha\cdot x=\beta\cdot P(x)]-\Pr_{x\leftarrow\mathbb{F}_2^n}[\alpha\cdot x\ne\beta\cdot P(x)]$, where $x$ is uniform. Set $v=\dim(V)$, $u=\dim\!\left(V\cap(\mathbb{F}_2^n\times\{0^n\})\right)$, and $w=\dim\!\left(V\cap(\{0^n\}\times\mathbb{F}_2^n)\right)$. Formally prove the conjecture that $2^n\sum_{(\alpha,\beta)\in V\setminus\{(0^n,0^n)\}}\operatorname{Cor}(P;\alpha,\beta)^2$ approximately follows a $\chi^2$ distribution with $2^v-2^u-2^w+1$ degrees of freedom. Only a plausibility explanation, rather than a formal proof, is currently available.

scope.domain: Probabilistic analysis of multidimensional linear correlations for random permutations in symmetric cryptanalysis.
assumptions: P is a randomly chosen permutation of F₂ⁿ.
V is any vector subspace of F₂ⁿ × F₂ⁿ.
The correlation probabilities use uniform x in F₂ⁿ.
parameters: n: dimension of the binary permutation domain
V: vector subspace indexing the input-output mask pairs
v, u, and w: dimensions of V and its two zero-coordinate intersections, determining the conjectured degrees of freedom
scope.unresolved_remainder: Give a formal proof that the scaled sum of squared nonzero-mask correlations approximately follows the stated chi-squared distribution.

citations.label: Quantum Speed-Up for Multidimensional (Zero Correlation) Linear Distinguishers

progress.summary: The source labels the distribution claim a conjecture and reports no formal proof, offering only a plausibility explanation in its appendix.
